office_does: A State Representative writes and votes on Washington state law and the operating, capital, and transportation budgets, covering school funding, the tax structure, housing rules, and criminal-justice statutes.
race_blurb: First-term Republican Brian Burnett, a former Chelan County sheriff, faces Democrat Stacy Willoughby, a Chelan banker and nonprofit president, after a primary decided by 174 votes districtwide. Most of the district is in Chelan County; Willoughby led the King County portion.

candidates.summary: First-term incumbent and three-term former Chelan County sheriff, running on public safety, spending restraint and local control.
highlights: Voted against ESSB 6346 (2026) and against ESHB 1296 (2025) [S4][S5]
Says he would have supported both 2026 initiatives on parental rights and girls' sports [S2]
Wants decision-making returned to local communities, including on housing [S1][S11]

taxes.basis: Voted against the 2026 income tax, issued a release criticizing it, and objects to record tax increases.

spending.basis: Says state spending has doubled and pledges budgeting that reins in spending; pamphlet stresses prioritizing taxpayer dollars.

safety.basis: Former sheriff whose platform is supporting law enforcement and holding offenders accountable.

local-control.basis: Pamphlet calls for returning decision-making to local communities; at a forum said the state should let cities decide on housing.

experience.basis: One legislative term plus twelve years as an elected sheriff, against a first-time candidate.

parental-rights.basis: Voted against ESHB 1296 twice, campaigns on protecting 'your role as a parent,' and says he would have supported the parental-rights initiative I-1 restores.

social.basis: Says he would have supported the girls' sports initiative (I-638) had it reached the floor; single explicit statement.

candidates.summary: First-time candidate from Chelan with 25 years in financial services and president of an anti-poverty nonprofit, running on housing, rural tax fairness and trades training.
highlights: Calls for "tax fairness for rural families and small businesses" [S1]
Would increase housing supply, cut permitting burdens, and invest in rural and workforce housing [S2]
Said communities should decide their own housing needs [S7]

spending.basis: Pairs investment in education, healthcare and infrastructure with 'fund what works, cut waste' budgeting.

housing.basis: Mixes supply-side permitting cuts with public investment in rural and workforce housing and limits on predatory lending.

local-control.basis: Said at a forum that each community should decide what it needs for housing.

experience.basis: First-time candidate who says government should work for everyday people, not party insiders.
